scope: Five remaining Grade5 Human Health/Body Systems source-duty residuals; ages10–11, source end-of-grade attainment. No PE or fitness curriculum is imported.
meaning: Original untested source-fit tasks; all actual duty types and conditions designed, no observed learner result or medical authority.

protocols.task: Compare the original three supplied cases below. Identify each social or environmental factor, explain a plausible body/well-being pathway, distinguish a support from a guarantee, and propose a feasible child-safe individual/adult/community response. Change access while holding personal health intentions constant; explain why identical advice is not equally usable.

cases.given: Two fictional families want a healthy home. One has a persistent leak and damp room; the other has dry repaired housing. A clinician has already identified asthma in one case. No pupil or family is described.
cases.expected: Housing conditions can affect breathing; a prepared adult can arrange repair/landlord/professional support. Not laziness, child mould removal or diagnosis from a cough.

cases.given: A fictional household has a nearby affordable food store and time to prepare meals; another has a long journey, limited budget and fewer suitable choices. Both want nutritious meals.
cases.expected: Availability, affordability, time and transport shape decisions; a suitable local food/school support and practical planning can help, but no child is responsible for fixing income or eliminating structural barriers.

cases.given: One new student has a safe trusted adult, welcoming peer contact and an accessible health-service appointment; another cannot yet access those supports.
cases.expected: Support/access can aid belonging and appropriate care; identify a safe adult/local resource and a welcoming action without claiming friendship cures disease or forcing disclosure.

protocols.positive: Connects varied access/environment/social factors to actual effects and feasible supports, including a benefit and a harm; goes beyond lifestyle slogans.
protocols.nearMiss: Says all health differences follow personal effort, labels a low-income family unhealthy, or gives adult repair/clinical responsibility to a child.
protocols.transfer: Change the barrier to language/accessibility or unsafe air while preserving the health goal; revise the action and explain who can act.

protocols.task: Use both original technology cases, identify the relevant organ/system and mechanism/purpose, weigh a benefit and limitation/risk for each, compare at least two actual stakeholder perspectives, and propose a feasible harm-reducing improvement. Judge the supplied case facts; do not diagnose, select treatment or handle a device.

cases.given: A fictional clinic uses a professionally justified digital bone image after an injury. The image helps a clinician see internal bone damage; radiation exposure has risk, and stored digital records need access/privacy protection. A family far from the clinic faces a travel barrier.
perspectives: patient/family needing understandable information and accessible care
clinician needing useful information with proportionate exposure
clinic responsible for privacy and suitable access
cases.expected: Skeletal information is a benefit; radiation/privacy/access are distinct limitations. Qualified clinicians decide clinical need. A child can suggest clearer explanation, protected access or help reaching an appointment, not self-authorise a scan.

cases.given: A professionally fitted hearing aid helps a fictional wearer hear speech. Busy-room noise can also be amplified, adjustment takes support and cost can affect access. The wearer says which situations work for them. A supplied adult-verified case report also describes irritation of the ear-canal skin from a device; this is a possible harm, not an inevitable result or a pupil diagnosis.
perspectives: wearer whose own communication preferences matter
teacher/peer who can reduce noise and check understanding
family/service supporting appropriate fitting and access
cases.expected: Auditory support is useful without restoring every hearing function. Respect the wearer’s preference; reduce background noise/access barriers. Do not assume every deaf person wants the same device or make a child fit one. Identify the supplied skin-irritation harm separately from cost/noise limitations and seek prepared-adult/professional support; do not adjust, trial or repair a medical device.

protocols.positive: Evaluates two technologies with correct health/body links, evidence and differing relevant perspectives; improvement addresses a stated limitation.
protocols.nearMiss: Lists device names only, says technology is always good/bad, treats digital storage as the entire health effect, or guesses a diagnosis/medicine.
protocols.transfer: Change the setting/access need and revise whose benefit/risk matters while retaining both medical-information and communication cases.

protocols.task: Use a concrete fictional day-menu and safe shared-meal planning case. Interpret guide/ingredient/marketing information, choose an affordable culturally suitable meal modification and explain a physical nutrient/function reason plus a different connection/enjoyment/routine reason. Explain how planning, knowing food and preparation options, and checking a message improve the decision. Identify uncertainty and who helps with medical/allergy needs. No food must be eaten and no private intake is scored.

case.menu: Breakfast oats with milk or suitable alternative and fruit; lunch rice with beans and vegetables; dinner a vegetable/legume dish with a grain option and water. This is an original planning case, not a prescribed individual diet or a universal menu.
case.choice: Compare a supplied colourful drink advert promising instant happiness with a factual water/variety recommendation. Change the budget, ingredient availability or social access; plan a feasible alternative and an optional safe way to share a meal/conversation.
case.expected: Foods support energy, growth/repair and body function; preparing/planning/checking claims can support informed choices and a positive relationship/connection. Neither one food nor a compulsory shared meal guarantees happiness or treats a mental-health condition.

protocols.positive: Explains food-literacy skills→reasoned decision→both physical and mental/social well-being pathways, with practical context and limits.
protocols.nearMiss: Names nutrients only, treats a paid happy-drink slogan as evidence, demands tasting/cheerfulness, or claims food replaces mental-health care.
protocols.transfer: Change cost, a suitable ingredient or eating arrangement; retain nutrition and voluntary connection reasons without one universal cultural/medical choice.

protocols.task: Complete all three underlying tasks, then explain one coherent fictional health scenario in which housing/food/service/social access, a technology and a food decision interact. Weigh both helpful and harmful effects and identify a feasible action plus its limits. The integration must use actual case details and a body/well-being explanation; a list of the three topic names or linked child counts is insufficient.
protocols.positive: Combines the different influences into a reasoned health account without blaming the individual or claiming a universal cure.
protocols.nearMiss: Repeats lifestyle advice while omitting the access condition, technology effect or mental/physical food-literacy connection.
protocols.transfer: Change one environmental or access condition; revise the plan and explain why the same personal intention may need different support.

protocols.task: Construct an original labelled body-system map and explain it orally, in writing or with labels/arrows. Cover the concrete organ/function set below, trace connected oxygen/nutrient/waste pathways, explain a deliberate senses→brain/nerves→muscle action without treating all automatic functions as conscious, and use all three supplied disorder cases to connect affected structures with function. Repair changed arrows/labels and transfer to a different everyday action. The learner produces the connected explanation; a supplied finished poster or one breathing answer is not the whole task. For every selected organ-structure pair, label or describe the actual basic physical feature and explain how it supports that organ’s job. Complete the changed-feature repair cases below; names, functions and route arrows alone do not pass the structure requirement.

functions: recover water and pass undigested waste
exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with blood
work together to move an ordinary object

pathways: air→lungs; oxygen enters blood; heart/vessels deliver it to cells; carbon dioxide returns in blood to lungs and leaves in exhaled air
food→mouth/oesophagus/stomach/intestines; absorbed nutrients enter transport routes and reach body parts; undigested material follows a different waste route
a seen cup→sensory messages→brain/nerves→arm/hand muscles moving it with skeletal support; no exercise curriculum or fitness norm

disorderCases.name: asthma
disorderCases.given: An already diagnosed fictional case has lung airways that can narrow/inflame.
disorderCases.expected: Respiratory system: changed airway function can make moving air harder; it is not a problem in the stomach.

disorderCases.name: tooth decay
disorderCases.given: Bacterial acids have damaged a fictional tooth’s enamel.
disorderCases.expected: Teeth/mouth support chewing in the digestive pathway; a tooth problem can impair that function. Do not examine anyone’s mouth or infer a diagnosis.

disorderCases.name: coronary heart disease
disorderCases.given: A supplied factual case describes reduced flow through vessels supplying the heart muscle.
disorderCases.expected: Circulatory system: the heart muscle needs its own oxygen/nutrient supply to pump well. Not every heart problem is the same and no child diagnoses symptoms.

protocols.positive: Shows structure/function within several systems, explains multiple inter-system connections, and places different named disorders in the correct organ/system model. Explicitly relates muscular/valved compartments, branching exchange structures and digestive wall/lining features to their functions, and repairs a changed feature with a reason.
protocols.nearMiss: Labels a heart without its function, sends whole food into blood, says arteries always mean oxygen-rich, confuses stool with carbon dioxide or merely says illness is bad. A poster of organ-name boxes connected by arrows, with no described physical structure-function relation, does not pass.
protocols.transfer: Reverse an oxygen/nutrient arrow or substitute an affected airway/heart-supply/tooth structure; repair it and explain the functional consequence. Repair at least one changed structural feature in a second organ/system rather than merely repeat a memorised route.

organStructureFunctionPairs.structure: muscular walls, chambers and one-way valves
organStructureFunctionPairs.function: Contraction moves blood through compartments; valves help prevent backward flow.
organStructureFunctionPairs.changedFeature: A model valve is drawn open both ways. Repair the arrows/valve and explain why directed pumping would be affected.

organStructureFunctionPairs.structure: branching airways ending in many small air sacs next to tiny blood vessels
organStructureFunctionPairs.function: Air reaches many exchange sites; oxygen moves to blood while carbon dioxide moves from blood to air.
organStructureFunctionPairs.changedFeature: The model ends its airway in a sealed large bag with no neighbouring blood-vessel exchange sites. Explain what essential structure-function relation is missing and repair it.

organStructureFunctionPairs.structure: muscular walls and a cavity receiving digestive juices
organStructureFunctionPairs.function: The walls mix food with juices, helping break it down before it moves onward.
organStructureFunctionPairs.changedFeature: A model stomach is only a rigid storage box. Add the missing mixing-wall action and explain why storage alone is insufficient.

organStructureFunctionPairs.structure: a tube with an absorbing lining
organStructureFunctionPairs.function: Digested nutrients cross the lining into transport routes instead of whole food entering blood.
organStructureFunctionPairs.changedFeature: The model lining is drawn as an impermeable barrier. Repair the nutrient-crossing relation and explain the consequence; do not require transport-protein or histology terminology.

resources.actualRead: Full main body About health equity/social/structural determinants/importance
resources.use: Access to housing, income, services, community support and freedom from discrimination shapes opportunity for health. Not individual blame or a requirement to disclose family resources.

resources.actualRead: Complete main body through About mould
resources.use: Damp housing and mould can worsen breathing/allergic problems. Prepared fictional facts only; children do not inspect, touch, smell, clean, grow or experimentally expose anyone to mould.

Internal pictures can help clinicians identify bone and other system problems. Radiation risks mean appropriate professional use, not child imaging/treatment decisions or a universal safe number of scans.

resources.actualRead: Complete benefits, limitations, doctor and reporting body
resources.use: Hearing aids can support communication; background noise, adjustment, cost and access remain limitations. No universal restoration, child fitting or transfer of US adult OTC policy.

resources.actualRead: Complete main body including family and older-adult sections
resources.use: Food decisions can support connection, enjoyment and eating routines. These are opportunities, not guaranteed feelings or mental-health treatment.

resources.actualRead: Full recommendations; also previously qualified in Health98 programme
resources.use: Variety, planning, food skills, guide/label interpretation and marketing awareness, with local access and personal medical/cultural conditions.
Heart pump, vessels, nutrient/oxygen transport, carbon-dioxide return and organ interdependence; no adult pulse/BMI/clinical score.

resources.actualRead: Complete main body including valves/double circulation/coronary supply
resources.use: Direction-defined vessels and correct body→right heart→lungs→left heart→body route. Advanced coronary branches/valve names are not extra Grade5 duties.

resources.actualRead: Complete main article, including digestion, absorption and neural/hormonal control. Linked videos were not viewed.
resources.use: Organ functions, nutrient absorption into transport systems, food waste and nervous/hormonal control. Nutrients have different routes; no all-absorption-by-diffusion or whole food entering blood.

resources.actualRead: Complete What Is Asthma main body
resources.use: A supplied diagnosed case affects lung airways, which may narrow/inflame; no symptom-based diagnosis or medicine instruction.
Bacterial acids can damage tooth enamel; teeth support the mouth’s mechanical digestive function. No dental examination, treatment or blame.

resources.actualRead: Complete respiratory-system main body, including airways, air sacs and exchange; separate lungs overview also read. No videos viewed.
resources.use: Branching tubes, small air sacs and adjacent vessels support opposite oxygen/carbon-dioxide movement. No numerical alveoli norm, advanced histology or universal gas formula. Nutrients originate from digestive absorption, not the lung airways.
